---
title: "Quickstart"
description: "From two public samples to a batch-corrected, clustered object."
order: 0
---

Run a best-practice single-cell pipeline end to end on two small public PBMC
samples: from per-sample count matrices to one filtered, normalized,
**batch-corrected and clustered** object. No prior Nextflow or single-cell
experience needed, every command is here.

This starts from **pre-computed counts**, so it skips the heavy alignment step and
runs in minutes. To do that mapping step yourself (raw FASTQ → counts with Cell
Ranger), see [Ingest data](../guides/ingest-10x.qmd).

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Before you start**

- **Prerequisites:** macOS, Linux, or Windows with WSL2, Nextflow needs a
  Unix-like environment. Python 3.11+ is used only for the inspection commands. No
  prior Nextflow or single-cell experience needed.
- **Hardware:** modest, the run is capped to 4 GB RAM per step (step 1), so any
  laptop works. The two samples are ~1,000 cells each.
- **Time:** about 15 minutes once set up; the first run also pulls Docker images,
  a one-time download.
- **What you'll have at the end:** one batch-corrected, Leiden-clustered `.h5mu`
  object with a UMAP, built from two PBMC samples.
:::

## 1 · Set up Nextflow and Docker {#sec-setup-nextflow-and-docker}

Everything else ships inside containers, so this is all you install: a Java
runtime (Nextflow needs it), Nextflow, and Docker.

**1a · Java prerequisite.** Commands per OS. Java 17+ is recommended (11 is the
minimum).

::: {.panel-tabset}

### macOS

```bash
# install Homebrew (https://brew.sh) first, then:
brew install openjdk@17
```

### Ubuntu / Debian

```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install openjdk-17-jdk unzip curl
```

### RHEL / Fedora

```bash
sudo yum install java-17-openjdk-devel unzip curl
```

### Arch

```bash
sudo pacman -Syy jdk17-openjdk unzip curl
```

### Windows

Use [WSL2](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/wsl/install) with Ubuntu, then
follow the Ubuntu / Debian commands above.

:::

Check it with `java -version`.

**1b · Nextflow.**

```bash
curl -s https://get.nextflow.io | bash
sudo mv nextflow /usr/local/bin/
nextflow -version
```

**1c · Docker.** Install [Docker Desktop](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/)
(macOS/Windows) or Docker Engine (Linux), start it, then check `docker --version`.

Finally, tell Nextflow where to pull the pipeline from (one time):

```bash
mkdir -p "$HOME/.nextflow"
cat >> "$HOME/.nextflow/scm" <<'EOM'
providers.vsh.platform = "gitea"
providers.vsh.server = "packages.viash-hub.com"
EOM
```

The demo data is tiny, so cap the pipeline's default resource requests, otherwise
a step may ask for more CPU or memory than a laptop has (the defaults are sized
for full-scale cohorts). Write a small Nextflow config, see
[Tune compute resources](../guides/tune-resources.qmd) for how these labels work:

```bash
cat > /tmp/demo.config <<'EOF'
process {
  withLabel: lowcpu      { cpus = 2 }
  withLabel: midcpu      { cpus = 2 }
  withLabel: highcpu     { cpus = 2 }
  withLabel: lowmem      { memory = 4.GB }
  withLabel: midmem      { memory = 4.GB }
  withLabel: highmem     { memory = 4.GB }
  withLabel: veryhighmem { memory = 4.GB }
}
EOF
```

## 2 · Get the data

Two small public PBMC samples, sequenced with different 10x chemistries, so they
carry a technical **batch effect** for the pipeline to correct. They come as
ready-made MuData (`.h5mu`) count objects, one per sample:

```bash
mkdir -p data && cd data
base="https://openpipelines-bio.s3.amazonaws.com/openpipeline_docs/data"
curl -O "$base/pbmc_1k_v2.h5mu"
curl -O "$base/pbmc_1k_v3.h5mu"
cd ..
```

Each file holds one sample's raw RNA counts. Open both in Python with the
[`mudata`](https://mudata.readthedocs.io/) package to see what's inside:

```bash
pip install 'mudata~=0.3.8' 'anndata~=0.12.16'   # matches openpipeline v4.2.0; needs Python >=3.11
for s in pbmc_1k_v2 pbmc_1k_v3; do
  echo "== $s =="
  python -c "import mudata; print(mudata.read_h5mu('data/$s.h5mu'))"
done
```

```
== pbmc_1k_v2 ==
MuData object with n_obs × n_vars = 996 × 33538
  var:  'gene_symbol', 'feature_types', 'genome'
  1 modality
    rna:  996 × 33538
      var:  'gene_symbol', 'feature_types', 'genome'
== pbmc_1k_v3 ==
MuData object with n_obs × n_vars = 1222 × 33538
  var:  'gene_symbol', 'feature_types', 'genome'
  1 modality
    rna:  1222 × 33538
      var:  'gene_symbol', 'feature_types', 'genome'
```

Two **separate** objects, one per sample, each a single `rna` modality of raw
counts (cells × genes) with gene metadata in `.var` and nothing computed yet.
Step 3 filters and **concatenates them into one** object (watch the cell count
grow as the two merge), and the later steps add normalized counts and embeddings
to it.

## 3 · Process the samples

`multiomics/process_samples` filters low-quality cells on each sample's own
distribution, then concatenates all samples and processes them together:
normalization, highly variable gene selection, PCA, and a neighbor graph and UMAP.
Write the sample list and QC thresholds to a params file, then run it:

```bash
cat > /tmp/params_process.yaml <<'EOF'
param_list:
  - id: pbmc_1k_v2
    input: data/pbmc_1k_v2.h5mu
  - id: pbmc_1k_v3
    input: data/pbmc_1k_v3.h5mu
rna_min_counts: 500           # thresholds you'd normally read off a QC report
rna_min_genes_per_cell: 200
max_fraction_mito: 0.2
output: pbmc_processed.h5mu
publish_dir: results/processed
EOF

nextflow run https://packages.viash-hub.com/vsh/openpipeline.git \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/multiomics/process_samples/main.nf \
  -params-file /tmp/params_process.yaml \
  -c /tmp/demo.config
```

Each entry is one **sample**; the `id` labels it and `input` points at its
`.h5mu`. The [Process many samples](../guides/process-many-samples.qmd) guide
covers the full `param_list` model, and [Generate a QC report](../guides/qc-report.qmd)
covers choosing the thresholds.

Inspect the result to see what processing added:

```bash
python -c "import mudata; print(mudata.read_h5mu('results/processed/pbmc_processed.h5mu'))"
```

```
MuData object with n_obs × n_vars = 2171 × 33538
  var:  'genome', 'filter_with_counts', 'gene_symbol', 'feature_types', 'filter_with_hvg', 'obs_mean', 'log1p_obs_mean', 'total_counts', 'log1p_total_counts', 'num_nonzero_obs', 'pct_dropout'
  1 modality
    rna:        2171 × 33538
      obs:      'filter_with_scrublet', 'filter_with_counts', 'scrublet_doublet_score', 'sample_id', 'num_nonzero_vars', 'log1p_num_nonzero_vars', 'total_counts', 'log1p_total_counts', 'pct_of_counts_in_top_50_vars', 'pct_of_counts_in_top_100_vars', 'pct_of_counts_in_top_200_vars', 'pct_of_counts_in_top_500_vars'
      var:      'genome', 'filter_with_counts', 'gene_symbol', 'feature_types', 'filter_with_hvg', 'obs_mean', 'log1p_obs_mean', 'total_counts', 'log1p_total_counts', 'num_nonzero_obs', 'pct_dropout'
      uns:      'log1p', 'neighbors', 'pca_variance'
      obsm:     'X_pca', 'X_umap'
      varm:     'pca_loadings'
      layers:   'log_normalized'
      obsp:     'connectivities', 'distances'
```

Both samples are now concatenated into one object; the cell count sits a little
below the two samples' combined total because low-quality cells were filtered out.
`.obs['sample_id']` records which initial sample each observation (cell) came
from, so even after merging you can tell them apart, and it's the column
integration corrects on next. Processing filled in much more besides: per-cell and
per-gene QC metrics (`total_counts`, `pct_dropout`, `scrublet_doublet_score`, …),
normalized counts in `.layers['log_normalized']`, the highly variable genes
flagged as `filter_with_hvg`, a PCA embedding in `.obsm['X_pca']`, and a neighbor
graph and UMAP (`.obsm['X_umap']`, `.obsp`), all computed on the uncorrected data.
Integration will redo the graph, clustering, and UMAP on the *corrected* space
next.

## 4 · Integrate

With two samples there's a batch effect to correct. `integration/harmony_leiden`
batch-corrects across samples on `sample_id`, then builds a neighbor graph,
clusters with Leiden, and computes a UMAP on the corrected embedding:

```bash
cat > /tmp/params_integrate.yaml <<'EOF'
id: pbmc_integrated
input: results/processed/pbmc_processed.h5mu
obs_covariates: sample_id
output: pbmc_integrated.h5mu
publish_dir: results/integrated
EOF

nextflow run https://packages.viash-hub.com/vsh/openpipeline.git \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/integration/harmony_leiden/main.nf \
  -params-file /tmp/params_integrate.yaml \
  -c /tmp/demo.config
```

To choose a different method (scVI, Scanorama, …) or compare several, see
[Integrate across samples](../guides/integrate.qmd).

## 5 · Read the output

Inspect the integrated object the same way:

```bash
python -c "import mudata; print(mudata.read_h5mu('results/integrated/pbmc_integrated.h5mu'))"
```

```
MuData object with n_obs × n_vars = 2171 × 33538
  var:  'genome', 'filter_with_counts', 'gene_symbol', 'feature_types', 'filter_with_hvg', 'obs_mean', 'log1p_obs_mean', 'total_counts', 'log1p_total_counts', 'num_nonzero_obs', 'pct_dropout'
  1 modality
    rna:        2171 × 33538
      obs:      'filter_with_scrublet', 'filter_with_counts', 'scrublet_doublet_score', 'sample_id', 'num_nonzero_vars', 'log1p_num_nonzero_vars', 'total_counts', 'log1p_total_counts', 'pct_of_counts_in_top_50_vars', 'pct_of_counts_in_top_100_vars', 'pct_of_counts_in_top_200_vars', 'pct_of_counts_in_top_500_vars', 'harmony_integration_leiden_1.0'
      var:      'genome', 'filter_with_counts', 'gene_symbol', 'feature_types', 'filter_with_hvg', 'obs_mean', 'log1p_obs_mean', 'total_counts', 'log1p_total_counts', 'num_nonzero_obs', 'pct_dropout'
      uns:      'harmonypy_integration_neighbors', 'log1p', 'neighbors', 'pca_variance'
      obsm:     'X_leiden_harmony_umap', 'X_pca', 'X_pca_integrated', 'X_umap'
      varm:     'pca_loadings'
      layers:   'log_normalized'
      obsp:     'connectivities', 'distances', 'harmonypy_integration_connectivities', 'harmonypy_integration_distances'
```

Integration added, on top of everything `process_samples` produced:

- `.obsm['X_pca_integrated']`, the batch-corrected embedding (Harmony).
- `.obs['harmony_integration_leiden_1.0']`, the cluster labels computed on that
  corrected embedding.
- `.obsm['X_leiden_harmony_umap']`, a UMAP of the corrected space, distinct from
  the uncorrected `X_umap` from step 3, plus its own neighbor graph
  (the `harmonypy_integration_*` entries in `.uns` / `.obsp`).

The clusters are just numbers so far. Assigning biological identities to them is
[cell type annotation](../guides/annotate.qmd), a separate step.
